hypothesis: The repository asserts more than one mutually exclusive 'recommended' production architecture, so a learner completing the Academy deploys something the canonical docs contradict.
evidence: README.md:191 heading '## Recommended production deployment' diagrams Firebase Hosting (frontend) -> Hostinger Node.js (server/ API) -> MongoDB Atlas, i.e. cross-origin.
docs/PRODUCTION_DEPLOYMENT.md:219-221 '## 5. Cross-origin contract' states 'The Firebase and Hostinger domains are intentionally separate.'
docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:21,70 documents a third stack: '## 1. Frontend - Vercel' and '## 2. Backend - Railway (Recommended)'.

public/deployment-guide.html:212 'Why this is the primary path: you already have a KVM 1, so serving both the static frontend and API from the same VPS keeps the first production deployment understandable and avoids an extra cross-origin hosting layer.'

Firebase/Vercel/Railway are never mentioned anywhere in deployment-guide.html; the guide's stated rationale explicitly rejects the cross-origin layer that README and PRODUCTION_DEPLOYMENT.md prescribe.
user_impact: A learner who completes all 24 Academy steps ends up on a single same-origin VPS. The repository's own canonical README then tells them that is not the recommended production deployment. There is no reconciliation text anywhere, so the learner cannot tell which path is authoritative, and CORS_ORIGINS / CLERK_AUTHORIZED_PARTIES guidance differs materially between the two.

hypothesis: docs/DEPLOYMENT.md is stale and contradicts current invariants, but was never removed or marked superseded.
evidence: Documents Vercel + Railway/Render/Fly.io, a stack no workflow, config or other doc references.
Not linked from README.md (README links only docs/PRODUCTION_DEPLOYMENT.md).
Predates the Clerk-canonical migration: server/routes/auth.js now returns HTTP 410 for signup/login/refresh, yet this doc still documents the legacy JWT_SECRET / JWT_REFRESH_SECRET model.
Documents MONGODB_URI as optional with SQLite fallback; README.md and server/server.js require Mongo in production.
user_impact: A reader who opens docs/DEPLOYMENT.md instead of docs/PRODUCTION_DEPLOYMENT.md - the filenames are near-identical - follows a retired architecture, sets env vars the server no longer reads, and is told Mongo is optional when production refuses to start without it.

hypothesis: The six-pass validator never inspects the artifact that actually ships, so the build-time patch is only verified after it is already public.
evidence: scripts/check-deployment-guide.mjs:10-13 reads exactly four paths: public/deployment-guide.html, index.html, src/index.jsx, src/components/SiteUtilityFooter.tsx. dist/ appears nowhere in the file.
vite.config.ts closeBundle() rewrites dist/deployment-guide.html in place, injecting the 'Shipping mobile containment gate' CSS.

.github/workflows/pages.yml greps the live URL for 'Shipping mobile containment gate' only AFTER actions/deploy-pages has published it.
user_impact: If the Vite transform regresses, every pre-merge gate stays green and the defect is caught only by a post-deploy grep on the live site, after users can already reach the broken page.

hypothesis: The guide is excluded from the repo's responsive-geometry matrix, so two of four contracted viewports are never checked on it.
evidence: e2e/layout-integrity.spec.ts:147 routes array lists only app routes (/tasks,/calendar,/budget,/social,/routines,/rewards,/settings,/pricing); deployment-guide.html is absent.
e2e/deployment-guide.spec.ts covers 320x568 and 390x844 only; 768x1024 and 1440x900 are never geometry-asserted for the guide.

Claude_changes.md has zero case-insensitive matches for hostinger, vps, kvm or deploy.

hypothesis: Re-adding the quick-start template tooltip during the origin/main merge broke upstream's 320px empty-state height budget.
evidence: e2e/tasks-best-in-class.spec.ts:94 asserts documentElement.scrollHeight <= 1900 at 320x568.
Measured with the tooltip and an inline-flex wrapper: 1912px; the template button rendered 61px (two lines) instead of 44px.
A flex + minWidth:0 variant made it worse: 1929px, button 78px (three lines).
Measured with upstream's exact arrangement (block wrapper, no template tooltip): 1895px, button 44px (one line).
Headroom in upstream's design is therefore only 5px; the tooltip costs 17px and cannot fit.
The rendered label comes from i18n ('tasks.tpl.showGallery' = 'Quick-start from proven tasks'), which is longer than the JSX default upstream sized against ('Browse quick-start tasks').
user_impact: At 320px the Tasks empty state grew past the contracted height, lengthening the first-run scroll on the narrowest supported screen.
root_cause: The merge treated the tooltip as a purely additive restoration, but upstream's task-capture redesign had set a tight measured height budget with ~5px of slack. Adding a row-consuming sibling to the button forced its i18n label to wrap.
rejected_alternatives: Raising the budget from 1900 to 1920 - forbidden by the review contract: never increase a tolerance to silence a failure.
Shortening the i18n label - would change user-facing copy in 9 locales to work around a layout defect.
Absolutely positioning the tooltip out of flow - hides a control from the layout and risks overlap at other widths.
implementation: Dropped only the quick-start template tooltip and restored upstream's block wrapper. The other 12 BudgetTooltip instances are retained; the four in the create form sit inside the collapsed showTaskDetails disclosure and cost zero height in the empty state.

hypothesis: The local Playwright suite cannot reproduce CI because a gitignored .env.local silently changes app auth behaviour.
evidence: Full local run: 35 failed / 79 passed. Every failure was a redirect to /gylio/sign-in (e.g. tasks-best-in-class.spec.ts:28 toHaveURL received 'http://localhost:5173/gylio/sign-in').
.env.local defines VITE_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY and is gitignored (.gitignore:11 '.env*.local'), so CI never has it.
With VITE_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY= emptied, the same spec went from 0/5 to 4/5, isolating one genuine failure (GYLIO-UX-006) from 34 environmental ones.
No spec, README or contributing note documents that the suite must be run with Clerk disabled.
reproduction: VITE_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY= npx playwright test  # environmental failures disappear
user_impact: A developer running the suite locally sees 35 red tests that are green in CI, and a real regression hides among them. This nearly masked GYLIO-UX-006.

hypothesis: The 1-minute configuration helper is placed before the learner can possibly know several of its values, and nothing routes them back once they can.
evidence: Helper sits at document position 3 (deployment-guide.html:226), above Phase 0 and all 24 steps.
3 of its 7 fields have no default and are unknowable at page load: DOMAIN, VPS_IP, LAPTOP_IP. The other 4 ship sensible defaults (deploy, the repo URL, main, /var/www/gylio).
LAPTOP_IP is only discoverable at step 06, VPS_IP at step 07 ('Confirm the VPS and record its IP'), DOMAIN typically at step 19 (DNS) though it is first consumed at step 16.
The literal string 'configuration' appears once in the file - its own heading. No step links back to the helper.
The only in-page anchor href in all 795 lines is the skip link href='#guide-main'.
user_impact: A first-time learner meets seven input fields before any instruction, cannot fill three of them, and later - on reaching step 06/07/16 - must manually scroll back up a very long document with no link, anchor or table of contents to get there.

hypothesis: A 24-step, multi-session deployment journey ships with no table of contents or in-page navigation.
evidence: Only one anchor href exists in the document (#guide-main, the skip link).
No nav landmark, no phase index, no step list, no 'back to top'.
Re-entry is served only by the sticky toolbar's 'Resume next step' button, which scrolls to the first unchecked step (deployment-guide.html:689-693).
Resume can never reach the pre-step sections (start-here, current-limitations, configuration, architecture), which sit above step-01.
user_impact: Orientation and re-entry depend on scrolling. A learner returning after hours cannot jump to a phase, and cannot return to the configuration helper or architecture diagram at all via any control.
rejected_alternatives: The Resume button partially mitigates this for forward progress and is a deliberate, reasonable re-entry affordance - the gap is backward/lateral navigation, not resumption.

hypothesis: REJECTED: unfilled personalization values render as empty strings, producing silently-broken copy-paste commands such as 'ssh root@'.
evidence: deployment-guide.html:655 renderTemplates falls back explicitly: template.replace(/{{([A-Z_]+)}}/g, (_, key) => escapeTokenValue(settings[key]) || `{{${key}}}`).
An unset value therefore renders the visible literal {{VPS_IP}}, not an empty string or 'undefined'.
escapeTokenValue coerces null/undefined via String(value ?? '').trim(), so no 'undefined' can leak.
reproduction: Load the guide with empty localStorage and read step 09's first code block: it shows 'ssh root@{{VPS_IP}}'.
user_impact: None as feared. A user who copies an unfilled command gets an obviously bogus placeholder and an immediate shell error, not a plausible-looking wrong command. This is a deliberate and sound fallback.

hypothesis: My merge resolution of PremiumGate dropped the feature name from the upgrade heading, breaking the premium-gate contract.
evidence: Pristine origin/main worktree passes e2e/app-audit.spec.ts 15/15; the merged branch failed 2 of the same tests - proving the failures were merge-caused, not environmental.

Upstream App.jsx:386 rendered <UpgradePrompt featureName={t(featureI18nKey)} /> and its call sites at :394/:399/:404 DO pass featureI18nKey. My earlier check of the already-conflicted merged file concluded no call site passed it, which was wrong.
upstream en.json upgrade.title = '{{feature}} is a premium feature'; the merged dictionary kept wip's 'Unlock full access', so the heading never named the gated feature.
app-audit.spec.ts:117 asserts heading /routines is a premium feature/i.
reproduction: git worktree add --detach <tmp> origin/main && (cd <tmp> && npm ci && VITE_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY= npx playwright test e2e/app-audit.spec.ts)  # 15 passed
VITE_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY= npx playwright test e2e/app-audit.spec.ts  # 2 failed on the merged branch
user_impact: A user hitting a locked feature saw a generic 'Unlock full access' panel that never said which feature was locked or why they had landed there.
root_cause: Two internally-consistent designs collided: wip's richer prompt (outcomes + free alternative + trial CTA) and upstream's feature-specific heading. The conflict resolution kept wip's component and wip's i18n value, silently discarding upstream's contextual heading, and no gate caught it because the assertion lives in Playwright rather than in the aggregated quality job.
rejected_alternatives: Relaxing app-audit.spec.ts to accept the generic heading - would weaken a test to match reduced behaviour.
Reverting wholesale to upstream's simpler prompt - would discard wip's deliberate conversion work (outcomes, free-alternative framing, try-once).
red_test: e2e/app-audit.spec.ts:108 and :183 failed on the merged branch, passed on origin/main
implementation: UpgradePrompt now renders t('upgrade.title', '{{feature}} is a premium feature', { feature: featureName }); en and es-PE upgrade.title updated to the interpolated form. wip's outcomes/free-alternative/try-once content is retained.
validation: npm run check:i18n green (placeholder parity holds for the new interpolation)

hypothesis: Interactive buttons carry aria-labels that replace rather than extend their visible text, violating WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.3 Label in Name.
evidence: 'See plans' button had aria-label 'View all plan options' - the accessible name did not contain the visible label, so getByRole('button', {name:/see plans/i}) could not find it and the click timed out after 30s.
'Start 10-day free trial' button had aria-label 'Start your 10-day free trial' - the inserted word 'your' means the visible string is not contained in the accessible name.
'Try this once, free' button had aria-label 'Try {{featureName}} once for free' - entirely different wording.
WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.3 (Level A): 'For user interface components with labels that include text or images of text, the name contains the text that is presented visually.'
reproduction: VITE_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY= npx playwright test e2e/app-audit.spec.ts:183  # locator.click timeout on the See plans button
user_impact: Speech-input users saying 'click See plans' or 'click Start 10-day free trial' would not activate those buttons, because the spoken visible label does not match the accessible name. This is the exact failure mode SC 2.5.3 exists to prevent, and it sat on the primary conversion path.
root_cause: aria-label was used as a place for richer marketing phrasing rather than as an accessible name, treating it as supplementary description. The repo had no lint rule or test asserting label-in-name, so only an unrelated Playwright locator surfaced it.
rejected_alternatives: Changing the test locator to match the aria-label - would encode the accessibility defect as the expected contract.
red_test: e2e/app-audit.spec.ts:190 timed out waiting for the See plans button
implementation: Removed the two redundant overriding aria-labels (visible text is already a good accessible name) and rewrote tryOnceAria to 'Try this once, free - {{featureName}}' so the accessible name contains the visible label. Dropped the now-unused seePlansAria/startTrialAria keys from en and es-PE.
